title: Blockbuster Passed on Netflix for $50 Million
description:
In 2000, blockbuster could have bought Netflix for 50 million dollars.

Sources:
- Wikipedia: Netflix: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix
- Wikipedia: Blockbuster LLC: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockbuster_LLC

From Wikipedia (Blockbuster LLC): in 2000 Blockbuster turned down a chance to buy the fledgling Netflix for $50 million; at its peak in 2004 it operated 9,094 stores; it filed for bankruptcy protection in 2010; one franchised store remains, in Bend, Oregon. From Wikipedia (Netflix): Netflix was founded by Marc Randolph and Reed Hastings as a DVD rental service on August 29, 1997; it introduced a monthly subscription in September 1999; in 2005 it shipped 1 million DVDs a day; streaming launched January 16, 2007; it has 325 million paid memberships as of 2026. Photos: Wikimedia Commons (credits below). Not financial advice.

scenes.narration: Blockbuster could have bought Netflix for 50 million dollars.
It passed. It had over 9,000 stores.
Netflix just mailed DVDs. Two founders and a red envelope.
But it charged one monthly price. Then it started streaming.
Today, Netflix has 325 million paid members. Blockbuster has only one store.
